name: Sunset Twice
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that you can watch the sun set at its foot, take the lift up, and watch it set again. In 2011 Dubai's clerics even ruled that people living above floor 80 must break the Ramadan fast two minutes later than the street below. Build high enough and you get a second sunset.

name: Wrong Sand
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The UAE sits in a desert and still imports sand. Desert grains are blown round and smooth by the wind, so they cannot hold concrete together. The towers were built with rougher sand brought in from elsewhere. Having a lot of something is not the same as having the right thing. Funny, true, and hard to forget.

name: Sushi Rain
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The green code that rains down the screen in The Matrix is sushi recipes. Its designer, Simon Whiteley, scanned the characters from his wife's Japanese cookbooks. Bending Spoons took the spoon from that film. This is the other secret in it: the most famous image of the digital world was made from something warm and human.

name: Signed Inside
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: In 1982 the team that built the first Macintosh signed a sheet of paper. Steve Jobs had the signatures moulded into the inside of every case, where no customer would ever look, because real artists sign their work. A name for a company that puts its name on everything it ships, even the parts nobody opens.

name: Floor 80
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: A number with a story, like 37signals. In 2011 Dubai's clerics ruled that in the Burj Khalifa, people living above floor 80 must break the Ramadan fast two minutes later than everyone on the ground. Up there the sun has not set yet. Floor 80 is the height where the rules change.

name: Borrowed Planes
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Emirates took off on 25 October 1985 with 10 million dollars and two planes borrowed from Pakistan's national airline, crews included. Today it is one of the biggest airlines in the world. The whole Dubai story in two words: start with what you can borrow, then build something nobody can ignore.

name: Sand Runway
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Dubai's airport opened in 1960 with a runway made of compacted sand, 1,800 metres of it. It is now the busiest international airport in the world. A name about taking off from whatever you have under your feet.

name: 80 Falcons
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: In 2017 a photo went around the world: 80 hooded falcons sitting in the seats of a Gulf airliner, each with its own ticket. Falcons here even carry their own passports. A number plus a noun, like 37signals, and a picture nobody forgets. Here even the strangest idea gets a boarding pass.

name: Penguins Upstairs
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Inside the Mall of the Emirates, a short walk from the shops, lives a colony of king and gentoo penguins. In a desert city where summer passes 45 degrees. Nobody finds it strange any more. This is the Mustard and Linen kind of name: ridiculous, true, and a reminder that here somebody always says yes to the idea.

name: Two Tortoises
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The first living beings to fly around the Moon were not astronauts. They were two tortoises, on the Soviet Zond 5 in September 1968, three months before Apollo 8. They came back alive. A name for a small team that gets there first without making noise about it.
